title: AI's 'please regulate us' push - safety sincerity vs regulatory capture, and the infosec/OSS backlash
source: Public record: Altman 2023 Senate testimony (licensing regime); Amodei essays + Anthropic RSP; SB 1047 fight; LeCun / a16z / open-source + infosec-community criticism; DataRepublican + 'follow the money' threads. Chronology overlay (structural; no financial-core edges). HONESTY: testimony, essays, bills, and funding are FACT; 'regulatory capture / moat / threat-inflation / framing-manipulation' is a CONTESTED interpretation - this block presents BOTH the labs' stated safety rationale AND the critics' case, attributed, and asserts neither as proven intent.

edges.notes: May 2023: Altman told the US Senate he WELCOMED regulation and proposed a federal LICENSING regime + a new agency for frontier AI - the archetypal 'please regulate us' moment (fact of testimony). Supporters read it as responsible; critics as an incumbent moat (both framings noted).

Anthropic CEO Amodei pairs existential-risk warnings (essays; 'a real chance things go catastrophically wrong') with support-for-regulation-with-conditions + the Responsible Scaling Policy - the 'pacing' posture (fact of statements/RSP; sincerity vs strategy contested).

The labs' regulate-us push is recoded by critics as REGULATORY CAPTURE: licensing + compute-threshold rules that raise compliance cost, entrench incumbents, and pre-empt competitors - while the labs simultaneously lobby against provisions that bind them (contested interpretation; the lobbying + the stated safety rationale are both documented).

Anthropic's 'we support smart regulation' + RSP-as-template is the clearest capture-critique target (safety rules modeled on the incumbent's own practices become the baseline); Anthropic frames it as raising the floor (both framings; 2026 pacing-as-cartel/Buist is the sharpest version - spec-buist-v-anthropic-pacing).

The concrete stake: licensing / liability / compute thresholds fall HARDEST on open-source + startups (who can't absorb compliance or carry model-liability) - so 'safety' rules can function as a barrier to the open ecosystem (contested; the differential burden is real, the intent is not adjudicated).

Meta's chief AI scientist Yann LeCun is the leading establishment voice FOR open-source AI + AGAINST doom framing - arguing open models are safer (auditable) + that closed 'safety' arguments serve incumbents (attributed opinion; his role + stance are fact).

LeCun is a prominent critic of AI-existential-risk framing ('preposterously overblown'), arguing it is threat-inflation that distracts from real present harms + justifies incumbent-friendly control (attributed opinion).

a16z (Andreessen/Horowitz) mobilized 'little tech' + open-source advocacy against SB 1047 + licensing regimes (Techno-Optimist Manifesto; heavy lobbying) - itself an interested party (VC portfolio) on the anti-regulation side (fact of advocacy; interests noted on BOTH sides).

The critique: EA/longtermist EXISTENTIAL-risk framing crowds out present-harm critiques (bias, surveillance, labor, concentration) + supplies the moral urgency for incumbent-shaped rules ('we might kill everyone -> license us') - the framing-manipulation claim (contested interpretation; cf the TESCREAL critique).

EA / longtermism is the intellectual source of the x-risk framing that drives the safety-regulation push - and (per the EA-money map) funds the labs' safety teams, the evaluators, AND the advocates pushing it (fact of lineage + funding; coordinated-intent unsupported).

DataRepublican + infosec-twitter 'follow the money' work traces the funding behind the regulate-us / pause push to the EA/Open-Phil network - the independent, adversarial cross-check feeding the capture critique (fact that the tracing exists; conclusions are her/their critical POV, verify vs 990s).

The OSS/local-AI community's anti-capture argument: open weights are already in the wild + de-censorable (the open-weight paradox), so frontier LICENSING can't deliver the safety it promises - it can only entrench incumbents while the capability diffuses anyway (attributed argument; the leak is demonstrated).

SB 1047 was the flashpoint: OSS developers + a16z argued its liability + kill-switch provisions would chill open model release; safety proponents said it only touched the largest frontier models - the same bill read as protection OR as capture (fact of the fight; both readings).
